criteria.pass_when: On a capable host, supplies an actual adjustable rate view with clear units and correct model; otherwise explicitly reports capability limits and provides a readable static fallback. Does not claim interactivity from an unrendered mockup or solely because a tool exists.
criteria.evidence: Actual artifact and host/tool events; check 0, 10 and 20 req/s yield 0, 0 and 600 requests. Mark unavailable interaction/rendering evidence unverified.

criteria.pass_when: Keeps the 60-second horizon, zero initial backlog and no burst/latency estimate visible. Does not label a model result an observed production measurement.
criteria.evidence: Visible controls, output and caveat checked against model.txt.

calibration_pairs.facts: Backlog starts at 0 requests. Over 60 seconds, incoming traffic is a constant 0 to 20 requests/second and service capacity is 10 requests/second. End backlog = max(0, incoming_rate - 10) * 60 requests. This is a deterministic model with no burst or latency estimate.
calibration_pairs.good: An adjustable 0–20 req/s view shows the 60-second backlog, with samples 0 → 0, 10 → 0 and 20 → 600 requests. It labels the zero initial backlog and excludes burst and latency estimates. The artifact is actually created and interaction is checked.
calibration_pairs.poor: A fixed screenshot shows 0 → 0, 10 → 0 and 20 → 600 requests and the same assumptions, although an adjustable renderer is available. The user must recompute intermediate rates.
calibration_pairs.distinction: These evaluator descriptions compare equally factual artifacts on a capable host. Inspect the actual artifact; descriptions and promises are not execution evidence.
